ForgeMCP 0.2.17 — Controlled Landscape reset

Checked October 24, 2026. BLOCKED — LOCAL OWNER APPROVAL PENDING. One bounded editing-session request was registered; no Landscape modification or save was performed. No Editor was launched, and no Engine/plugin file, Original Layer, unrelated asset, or historical checkpoint was changed.

Editor and current Landscape

Fresh ForgeMCP discovery authenticated unreal-33500 / PID 33500, UE 5.6.1-44394996+++UE5+Release-5.6, ForgeMCP 0.2.17-alpha.1, project [local path], world /Game/Levels/L_City_World_Master.L_City_World_Master, PIE stopped. Landscape GUID BD45FDD94EC2A29617B50794F2DE4E9D; World Partition active, 16 loaded/0 unloaded streaming proxies, 64 registered Landscape components and 64 registered collision components. Layers are current and Landscape reports clean.

Original Layer GUID 198824024FF8A77A01535B86021D9B34, full-height MD5 9f43572fbc2c06ef497da015879cdb23, remains 0/0 local cm, visible/unlocked. ForgeTerrain GUID 2E6FC5F94C4EF704F700299B5D08C23B, full-height MD5 f5a8d55a3372fefe6fcadb0e7ff25b07, -100/0 local cm, visible/unlocked. Complete native dirty-package scan inspected 1,192 loaded packages with no error or further pages; only compiled-in /Script/SlateCore was dirty. Zero loaded production Content packages were dirty; unloaded packages were not classified.

New pre-change recovery checkpoint

[local path] is a new checkpoint, separate from all historical copies. It contains the current L_City_World_Master.umap and all 22 files then present in that map's __ExternalActors__ namespace: 23 files total. No __ExternalObjects__ namespace existed at inspection. Each source and copied file was SHA-256/size verified after copy; zero mismatches, missing files or membership exceptions were observed for this enumerated scope. The manifest pin is SHA-256 41ad3a15a126a4b2a3abe95ec796fa215388fc317504b20703c6d2403395baf4. Checkpoint files were marked read-only. The source files remained hash-identical after copying. This is a disk-file checkpoint, not an independent live-memory serialization or disk-reload proof.

Historical ForgeMCP approval checkpoint Saved/ForgeLandscapeAdoption/E1E328994273443311FB4A880BC326BE/manifest.json still matched its recorded SHA-256 f77b772e73774f1516b9fb94ecfd73584ccffa482ecabd92bc92e400a9181ed5 in the preceding delta investigation; its backup payloads were not rehashed in this run. No checkpoint was restored or overwritten.

Experimental sculpt isolation

The first live riverbed report [not indexed] established a flat, zero-height ForgeTerrain baseline with full MD5 equal to the Original Layer (9f43572fbc2c06ef497da015879cdb23) before its authorized apply_heightmap job. Its write region was [1055,1067,1085,1073] and created 101 negative samples. The two-extension execution [not indexed] records left [1043,1068,1057,1074] and right [1083,1066,1097,1072], 60 new negative vertices each under one later approval. Those are the only three retained ForgeMCP Landscape job directories found under Saved/ForgeLandscape; this is not a complete audit of every possible human or Editor action.

A fresh native ForgeTerrain read of the union plus one-vertex halo, [1042,1065,1098,1075] (627 samples), returned MD5 0bce98df53283065e7a173d2d0c56d73. Against the retained two-extension expected array, 603 samples match and 24 differ: x=1085–1096, y=1070–1071 of the right extension were previously negative and now read zero. Every current nonzero sample in this bounded read (197 total) lies inside the union of the three confirmed ForgeMCP write regions; the halo has zero nonzero samples. All 101 original riverbed samples, 60 left-extension samples, and 36 remaining right-extension samples are intact in this region. This supports an exact bounded restoration of the confirmed ForgeMCP sculpt to its verified zero-height ForgeTerrain baseline, leaving the 24 already-zeroed samples at zero. It does not justify a global flatten or changing Original Layer.

The owner's later manual brush work, Undo and save explain why the two-extension snapshot cannot be assumed current; the available evidence does not identify the operation that zeroed those 24 heights. The two additional indentations have no verified ForgeMCP job, location or expected-height record in the reviewed evidence. They are therefore excluded from the reset scope and must be preserved as unidentified/manual terrain. The full current ForgeTerrain hash differs from the two-extension hash, so differences outside this bounded region remain unlocalized. The reset plan does not touch those areas.

Reset method and authorization status

Proposed native method: one bounded apply_heightmap supplying exact zero local-centimeter values for the inclusive combined write rectangle [1043,1066,1097,1074] (55 × 9 = 495 samples), with authorization/readback halo [1042,1065,1098,1075]. Before any apply, reread the entire halo, require the same current sample array/MD5, verify all proposed changed vertices are exactly the 197 current negative samples associated with the three recorded ForgeMCP sculpts, and require every untouched halo/sample to match. Review the native preview's exact before/after array, normal halo, predicted package/height effects and session binding. A preview has not yet been generated; native production preview requires a valid local editing grant. Do not apply if the baseline changes, ownership is ambiguous, or preview disagrees.

Read-only unreal_landscape_edit_session_preflight passed for the correct Editor PID, actor, Landscape/layer GUIDs, World Partition, bounded region and apply_heightmap action. It reported clean checkpoint source, target layer ready/visible/unlocked, readable 23-file backup scope, and no readiness blocker. Exactly one request was registered:

  • Edit session ID: 672FB6EC401392B74E67AF852B57A393.
  • State at request: pending_local_approval; approved=false has not been established.
  • Scope: apply_heightmap only, ForgeTerrain GUID 2E6FC5F94C4EF704F700299B5D08C23B, bounded halo [1042,1065,1098,1075], Landscape GUID above, project/world above, Editor PID 33500, requested lifetime 3,600 seconds.
  • Local owner command: Forge.Landscape.ApproveEditSession 672FB6EC401392B74E67AF852B57A393 in the existing, identity-verified Unreal Editor. The owner must inspect the native confirmation before approving. This report is not approval.

No preview, apply, job, restore or save was called. If the request expires, is denied or cannot be verified, stop and report that state before creating another request. If locally approved, first verify status and the native checkpoint, then perform the exact preview and readback gates above. Saving the resulting Landscape packages requires a separate owner authorization; do not use Save All. An independent reload also requires separate approval. The current work has no post-reset modified package list because no edit occurred.

Validation and city-terrain readiness

After an authorized apply, acceptance would require a 495-sample zero readback plus unchanged halo, ForgeTerrain full-height hash checked against the expected result (not assumed in advance because other unidentified terrain may exist), Original Layer MD5 unchanged, Landscape GUID/material/layer identity unchanged, 16 proxies and 64/64 component registration, and complete dirty-package ownership. Then obtain separate approval for an exact-package save; verify file writes and hashes and later independently reload a copied saved project before claiming disk persistence. No reset-complete claim follows from a clean viewport alone.

The next demonstrations remain proposals only: mountain ridge (raise, candidate region after identifying both manual indentations), natural valley (lower), river system (lower/smooth), coastal slope (coastline), and smoothing refinement (smooth). Each needs a newly selected loaded/unused bounded region, numeric preview and protective halo, new recovery checkpoint, local edit approval, separate exact-package save approval, and independent disk-reload verification. New terrain development is not ready until this bounded reset is actually approved, applied, validated and saved, and the unidentified indentations are accounted for.

Local approval attempt — refused

The owner entered Forge.Landscape.ApproveEditSession 672FB6EC401392B74E67AF852B57A393 in the existing Editor. Its current log records: Landscape adoption refused: request stale or unsaved/unsafe world. Fresh native status for that exact ID reports approved=false, revoked=false, expired=false, expires_at_unix=0, backup_root empty, no active operation and operations=[]. Read-only preflight lists the request as approved=false/used=false with no native checkpoint files. No preview, apply, terrain edit or save followed.

Fresh discovery still authenticates unreal-33500 / PID 33500, the correct project/level/plugin and PIE stopped. A new complete loaded-package inventory inspected 1,192 packages and again found only compiled-in /Script/SlateCore dirty. A fresh read-only preflight again reports no current readiness blocker and readable 23-file backup scope. These observations do not establish which condition caused the local rejection. The warning groups stale request and unsaved/unsafe-world possibilities; neither is proven individually. Do not re-enter the command as though approval succeeded, create a replacement request, or apply terrain from this ID. The request is a failed/unverified authorization boundary pending a separate diagnosis and new owner decision.
